tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

445	def border_distance(me, co, adj, head, signed):
446	    """Distance (m) of each vert from a smooth skin-to-collar border, positive on the skin.
447	
448	    Close to the painted border the skin flag is averaged over the surface by area; across a straight border that
449	    average is the normal distribution of the distance, so its inverse is a distance again, and one that is linear
450	    along an edge however long the edge is. Zero of that field does not follow the edges of the mesh.
451	    """
452	    area = np.zeros(len(co))
453	    me.calc_loop_triangles()
454	    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
455	        for k in lt.vertices:
456	            if k < len(co):
457	                area[k] += lt.area / 3
458	    span = [[float(np.linalg.norm(co[a] - co[b])) for b in nb] for a, nb in enumerate(adj)]
459	    limit = 2.5 * NECK_BLUR
460	    side = head.astype(float)
461	    close = np.abs(signed) < NECK_REACH
462	    for i in np.where(close)[0]:
463	        dist = {int(i): 0.0}
464	        heap = [(0.0, int(i))]
465	        while heap:
466	            d, a = heapq.heappop(heap)
467	            if d > dist[a]:
468	                continue
469	            for b, step in zip(adj[a], span[a]):
470	                nd = d + step
471	                if nd < limit and nd < dist.get(b, limit):
472	                    dist[b] = nd
473	                    heapq.heappush(heap, (nd, b))
474	        near = np.fromiter(dist.keys(), dtype=np.int64)
475	        weight = area[near] * np.exp(-0.5 * (np.fromiter(dist.values(), dtype=float) / NECK_BLUR) ** 2)
476	        side[i] = (weight * head[near]).sum() / weight.sum()
477	    normal = statistics.NormalDist()
478	    smooth = np.array([NECK_BLUR * normal.inv_cdf(min(max(s, 0.005), 0.995)) for s in side])
479	    smooth = np.where(close, smooth, signed)
480	    # A vert right on the border would make faces that lie on both sides.
481	    return np.where(np.abs(smooth) < 1e-4, 1e-4, smooth)

def border_distance(me, co, adj, head, signed):
    """Distance (m) of each vert from a smooth skin-to-collar border, positive on the skin.

    Close to the painted border the skin flag is averaged over the surface by area; across a straight border that
    average is the normal distribution of the distance, so its inverse is a distance again, and one that is linear
    along an edge however long the edge is. Zero of that field does not follow the edges of the mesh.
    """
    area = np.zeros(len(co))
    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        for k in lt.vertices:
            if k < len(co):
                area[k] += lt.area / 3
    span = [[float(np.linalg.norm(co[a] - co[b])) for b in nb] for a, nb in enumerate(adj)]
    limit = 2.5 * NECK_BLUR
    side = head.astype(float)
    close = np.abs(signed) < NECK_REACH
    for i in np.where(close)[0]:
        dist = {int(i): 0.0}
        heap = [(0.0, int(i))]
        while heap:
            d, a = heapq.heappop(heap)
            if d > dist[a]:
                continue
            for b, step in zip(adj[a], span[a]):
                nd = d + step
                if nd < limit and nd < dist.get(b, limit):
                    dist[b] = nd
                    heapq.heappush(heap, (nd, b))
        near = np.fromiter(dist.keys(), dtype=np.int64)
        weight = area[near] * np.exp(-0.5 * (np.fromiter(dist.values(), dtype=float) / NECK_BLUR) ** 2)
        side[i] = (weight * head[near]).sum() / weight.sum()
    normal = statistics.NormalDist()
    smooth = np.array([NECK_BLUR * normal.inv_cdf(min(max(s, 0.005), 0.995)) for s in side])
    smooth = np.where(close, smooth, signed)
    # A vert right on the border would make faces that lie on both sides.
    return np.where(np.abs(smooth) < 1e-4, 1e-4, smooth)


def plain_black_uv(bm, uv, shirt):
    """One texel of plain black shirt, far from any seam."""
    donor = next(f for f in bm.faces if all(v.index < len(shirt) and shirt[v.index] and abs(v.co.x) > 0.15
                                             and v.co.y < -0.2 and 1.6 < v.co.z < 1.9 for v in f.verts))
    return sum((l[uv].uv for l in donor.loops), Vector((0, 0))) / len(donor.loops)


def covered(p, w, h, tol):
    """Texels under a UV triangle given in texel units: the slices of the block and the mask inside it."""
    x0, y0 = np.floor(p.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
    x1, y1 = np.ceil(p.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
    d = (p[1, 1] - p[2, 1]) * (p[0, 0] - p[2, 0]) + (p[2, 0] - p[1, 0]) * (p[0, 1] - p[2, 1])
    if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0 or abs(d) < 1e-9:
        return None
    xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
    b0 = ((p[1, 1] - p[2, 1]) * (xs - p[2, 0]) + (p[2, 0] - p[1, 0]) * (ys - p[2, 1])) / d
    b1 = ((p[2, 1] - p[0, 1]) * (xs - p[2, 0]) + (p[0, 0] - p[2, 0]) * (ys - p[2, 1])) / d
    tol = min(0.5, tol / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
    return slice(y0, y1 + 1), slice(x0, x1 + 1), (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (1 - b0 - b1 >= -tol)


def neck_border(mesh, co, adj, rgb, head, shirt, other, black_shirt, inside, out):
    """Cut a clean skin-to-collar border into the mesh.

    Meshy paints that border across the faces, ragged, with black spilled onto the jowls and skin onto the collar,
    and the faces in the crease are slivers with a few stretched texels each: it shows as a hairy fringe as soon as
    the head turns. The faces near the border are cut along a smooth line over the surface; on the collar side they
    turn plain black, on the skin side whatever is not skin is painted over. A face that reaches the jacket keeps
    its texture, with the skin on its collar side painted black. Faces with a vert of `other` are left alone.
    """
    me = mesh.data
    n = len(head)
    band = np.where(head, inside, out) < NECK_BAND
    side = border_distance(me, co, adj, head, np.where(head, inside, -out))
    near_skin = head & (inside < 0.10) & (rgb.max(axis=1) > 0.4)
    tone = np.median(rgb[near_skin], axis=0)

    def is_skin(c, colour=0.2):
        hi, lo = c.max(axis=-1), c.min(axis=-1)
        return (hi > 0.5) & ((hi - lo) > colour * hi) & (c[..., 0] >= c[..., 1])

    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_mesh(me)
    bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.active
    black_uv = plain_black_uv(bm, uv, black_shirt)
    faces = [f for f in bm.faces if all(v.index < n and not other[v.index] for v in f.verts)
             and any(band[v.index] for v in f.verts)]
    value = {v: float(side[v.index]) for f in faces for v in f.verts}
    mixed = {v for v in value if not (head[v.index] or shirt[v.index])}
    fresh = set()
    for e in {e for f in faces for e in f.edges}:
        a, b = e.verts
        sa, sb = value[a], value[b]
        if sa * sb >= 0:
            continue
        t = min(max(sa / (sa - sb), 0.05), 0.95)
        where = a.co.lerp(b.co, t)
        v = bmesh.utils.edge_split(e, a, t)[1]
        if (v.co - where).length > 1e-5:
            raise RuntimeError("edge_split measures from the other end")
        value[v] = 0.0
        fresh.add(v)
    # Each cut face gets an edge along the border; a neighbour that only received a vert is closed with a fan.
    for f in list({f for v in fresh for f in v.link_faces}):
        on = [v for v in f.verts if v in fresh]
        if len(on) == 2:
            bmesh.utils.face_split(f, on[0], on[1])
        elif len(on) == 1 and len(f.verts) == 4:
            ring = list(f.verts)
            bmesh.utils.face_split(f, on[0], ring[(ring.index(on[0]) + 2) % 4])
    bmesh.ops.triangulate(bm, faces=list({f for v in fresh for f in v.link_faces if len(f.verts) > 3}))

    image = base_image(me)
    w, h = image.size
    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    size = np.array((w, h))
    skin, collar = [], []
    for f in {f for v in value for f in v.link_faces}:
        if all(v in value for v in f.verts) and any(v in fresh or band[v.index] for v in f.verts):
            (skin if sum(value[v] for v in f.verts) > 0 else collar).append(f)
    texels = 0
    black_px = np.array((0.015, 0.015, 0.015))
    for f in collar:
        hit = covered(np.array([l[uv].uv[:] for l in f.loops]) * size - 0.5, w, h, 1.5)
        if any(v in mixed for v in f.verts):
            if hit:
                block = px[hit[0], hit[1], :3]
                block[hit[2] & is_skin(block, 0.3)] = black_px
            continue
        # These faces leave their texels; next to the border those texels still bleed into the skin faces.
        if hit and any(v in fresh for v in f.verts):
            block = px[hit[0], hit[1], :3]
            block[hit[2]] = tone
        for l in f.loops:
            l[uv].uv = black_uv
    for f in skin:
        hit = covered(np.array([l[uv].uv[:] for l in f.loops]) * size - 0.5, w, h, 1.5)
        if hit:
            block = px[hit[0], hit[1], :3]
            own = block[hit[2] & is_skin(block)]
            if any(v in mixed for v in f.verts):
                wrong = hit[2] & (block.max(axis=-1) < 0.25)
            else:
                wrong = hit[2] & ~is_skin(block)
            block[wrong] = np.median(own, axis=0) if len(own) >= 4 else tone
            texels += int(wrong.sum())
    first = len(me.vertices)
    bm.to_mesh(me)
    bm.free()
    image.pixels.foreach_set(px.ravel())
    image.update()
    image.pack()

    # A vert made by the cut carries the weights of both ends of its edge: back to four influences.
    for i in range(first, len(me.vertices)):
        groups = sorted(me.vertices[i].groups, key=lambda g: -g.weight)
        total = sum(g.weight for g in groups[:4])
        for k, g in enumerate([(g.group, g.weight) for g in groups]):
            if k < 4:
                mesh.vertex_groups[g[0]].add([i], g[1] / total, "REPLACE")
            else:
                mesh.vertex_groups[g[0]].remove([i])
    print("[build] neck border: %d verts cut in, %d skin faces, %d collar faces turned black, %d texels to skin, "
          "tone %s, %d verts in all" % (len(me.vertices) - first, len(skin), len(collar), texels, tone.round(3),
                                        len(me.vertices)))


def gild_knot(mesh):
    """Paint the top of the knot gold.

    Meshy left it dark, with a dot of skin, under two tips of the collar: it reads as a hole in the knot. Every texel
    whose place on the surface lies in the box of KNOT_CAP takes the gold of the knot below it, so the edge of the
    paint is straight whatever the faces are. A face whose texture was already folded into one texel moves whole.
    """
    me = mesh.data
    half, front, low, high = KNOT_CAP
    image = base_image(me)
    w, h = image.size
    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    size = np.array((w, h))
    uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
    co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
    me.calc_loop_triangles()

    def in_cap(p):
        return (np.abs(p[..., 0]) < half) & (p[..., 1] < front) & (p[..., 2] > low) & (p[..., 2] < high)

    # The gold of the knot right under the cap, and one texel that has it.
    samples = []
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        p = co[list(lt.vertices)]
        if np.all((np.abs(p[:, 0]) < 0.03) & (p[:, 1] < -0.15) & (p[:, 2] > 2.12) & (p[:, 2] < low)):
            spot = sum((uv[l].uv for l in lt.loops), Vector((0, 0))) / 3
            c = px[min(int(spot.y * h), h - 1), min(int(spot.x * w), w - 1), :3]
            if c[0] > 0.5 and c[1] > 0.6 * c[0] and c[2] < 0.6 * c[0]:
                samples.append((c.copy(), spot))
    gold = np.median([c for c, _ in samples], axis=0)
    gold_uv = min(samples, key=lambda s: float(np.abs(s[0] - gold).sum()))[1]

    texels = moved = 0
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        p = co[list(lt.vertices)]
        if not (p[:, 0].min() < half and p[:, 0].max() > -half and p[:, 1].min() < front
                and p[:, 2].min() < high and p[:, 2].max() > low):
            continue
        t = np.array([uv[l].uv[:] for l in lt.loops]) * size - 0.5
        hit = covered(t, w, h, 1.5)
        if hit is None or np.ptp(t, axis=0).max() < 0.5:
            if in_cap(p.mean(axis=0)):
                for l in lt.loops:
                    uv[l].uv = gold_uv
                moved += 1
            continue
        ys, xs = np.mgrid[hit[0], hit[1]]
        d = (t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (t[0, 1] - t[2, 1])
        b0 = ((t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
        b1 = ((t[2, 1] - t[0, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
        place = b0[..., None] * p[0] + b1[..., None] * p[1] + (1 - b0 - b1)[..., None] * p[2]
        mask = hit[2] & in_cap(place)
        block = px[hit[0], hit[1], :3]
        block[mask] = gold
        texels += int(mask.sum())
    image.pixels.foreach_set(px.ravel())
    image.update()
    image.pack()
    print("[build] knot cap: %d texels to gold %s, %d folded faces moved" % (texels, gold.round(3), moved))


def split_tie(mesh, co, W, names, tie, knot, shirt):
    """Cut the tie loose from the shirt it is modelled into.

    The tie faces are copied as a free two-sided strip that keeps the tie weights; the faces they came from stay on
    the body as plain black shirt, so nothing stretches between the two when the tie swings away. The faces that
    join the knot to the strip turn plain gold and stay where they are: black or sunk, they show as a wedge under
    the knot.
    """
    me = mesh.data
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_mesh(me)
    bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
    bm.normal_update()
    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.active
    faces = [f for f in bm.faces if all(tie[v.index] for v in f.verts)]
    join = [f for f in bm.faces if any(tie[v.index] for v in f.verts) and any(knot[v.index] for v in f.verts)]
    held = {v for f in join for v in f.verts}
    touching = [f for f in bm.faces if any(tie[v.index] for v in f.verts) and f not in join]
    black_uv = plain_black_uv(bm, uv, shirt)
    donor = min(faces, key=lambda f: (f.calc_center_median() - Vector(TIE_MID)).length)
    gold_uv = sum((l[uv].uv for l in donor.loops), Vector((0, 0))) / len(donor.loops)

    def outward(v):
        """Off the chest, never sideways: the folds of the knot have walls that would slide across the strip."""
        d = Vector((0.0, min(v.normal.y, -0.3), v.normal.z))
        return d.normalized()

    front = bmesh.ops.duplicate(bm, geom=faces)["geom"]
    back = bmesh.ops.duplicate(bm, geom=faces)["geom"]
    for geom, lift in ((front, TIE_LIFT), (back, 0.5 * TIE_LIFT)):
        for v in geom:
            if isinstance(v, bmesh.types.BMVert):
                v.co += outward(v) * lift
    bmesh.ops.reverse_faces(bm, faces=[f for f in back if isinstance(f, bmesh.types.BMFace)])
    # The shirt under the strip sinks, so a breathing belly does not come through the tie.
    for v in {v for f in faces for v in f.verts} - held:
        v.co -= outward(v) * TIE_SINK

    under = [f for f in faces if min(v.co.z for v in f.verts) > TIE_GOLD_UNDER]
    touching = [f for f in touching if f not in under]
    for group, spot in ((touching, black_uv), (join + under, gold_uv)):
        for f in group:
            for l in f.loops:
                l[uv].uv = spot
    bm.to_mesh(me)
    bm.free()

    # The verts left behind move like the shirt around them.
    body = np.where(shirt)[0]
    tree = kdtree.KDTree(len(body))
    for k, i in enumerate(body):
        tree.insert(co[i], k)
    tree.balance()
    groups = [mesh.vertex_groups[name] for name in names]
    for i in np.where(tie)[0]:
        near = [body[k] for _, k, _ in tree.find_n(co[i], 6)]
        row = W[near].mean(axis=0)
        row = np.where(row >= np.sort(row)[-4], row, 0.0)
        row /= row.sum()
        for g, value in zip(groups, row):
            if value > 0:
                g.add([int(i)], float(value), "REPLACE")
            else:
                g.remove([int(i)])
    print("[build] tie split: %d faces copied twice, %d turned black, %d gold under the knot, %d verts in all" % (
        len(faces), len(touching), len(join), len(me.vertices)))


def clean_actions(arm):
    """Meshy names are 'Armature|Idle'; curves of the dropped bones and of the armature object itself go."""
    bones = {b.name for b in arm.data.bones}
    for action in list(bpy.data.actions):
        action.name = action.name.split("|")[-1]
        removed = 0
        for layer in action.layers:
            for strip in layer.strips:
                for slot in action.slots:
                    bag = strip.channelbag(slot)
                    if bag is None:
                        continue
                    for fc in list(bag.fcurves):
                        path = fc.data_path
                        name = path.split('"')[1] if path.startswith("pose.bones[") else None
                        if name is None or name not in bones:
                            bag.fcurves.remove(fc)
                            removed += 1

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, writes the FBX files of Art/Models/boss_fixed).

Exports the reworked Publisher for Unreal: SK_Publisher.fbx (mesh, skeleton, embedded textures, no animation) and one
armature-only FBX per clip, named as the clip. The data is converted to centimetres first (rest bones, mesh and
location keys times 100, scene unit 0.01), so the file has unit scale 1 and no scaled armature node: root motion
comes into Unreal in true size whatever the importer does with units.

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/export_fbx.py -- <clips.blend> <out_dir> [probe.json]

probe.json receives world positions (cm) of every bone at a few frames of every clip, for verify_fbx.py.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import bpy

SCALE = 100.0
MESH_FILE = "SK_Publisher.fbx"


def fcurves(action):
    for layer in action.layers:
        for strip in layer.strips:
            for bag in strip.channelbags:
                yield from bag.fcurves


def to_centimetres(scene, arm, mesh):
    scene.unit_settings.system = "METRIC"
    scene.unit_settings.scale_length = 1.0 / SCALE
    arm.animation_data.action = None
    for pb in arm.pose.bones:
        pb.matrix_basis.identity()
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
    # The mesh is a child of the armature and takes its scale from it.
    assert mesh.parent == arm
    height = mesh.dimensions.z
    arm.scale = (SCALE, SCALE, SCALE)
    for ob in (arm, mesh):
        ob.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = arm
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
    assert abs(mesh.dimensions.z - height * SCALE) < 0.01 * height * SCALE, mesh.dimensions.z
    assert all(abs(s - 1) < 1e-6 for ob in (arm, mesh) for s in ob.matrix_world.to_scale())
    for action in bpy.data.actions:
        for fc in fcurves(action):
            if fc.data_path.endswith(".location"):
                for key in fc.keyframe_points:
                    key.co[1] *= SCALE
                    key.handle_left[1] *= SCALE
                    key.handle_right[1] *= SCALE
                fc.update()


def export(path, objects, animated):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
    for ob in objects:
        ob.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = objects[0]
    bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(
        filepath=path, use_selection=True, object_types={"ARMATURE", "MESH"}, global_scale=1.0,
        apply_unit_scale=True, apply_scale_options="FBX_SCALE_NONE", axis_forward="-Z", axis_up="Y",
        add_leaf_bones=False, primary_bone_axis="Y", secondary_bone_axis="X", use_armature_deform_only=False,
        armature_nodetype="NULL", mesh_smooth_type="FACE", use_tspace=False, use_mesh_modifiers=True,
        bake_anim=animated, bake_anim_use_all_bones=True, bake_anim_use_nla_strips=False,
        bake_anim_use_all_actions=False, bake_anim_force_startend_keying=True, bake_anim_step=1.0,
        bake_anim_simplify_factor=0.0, path_mode="COPY", embed_textures=not animated)


def main():
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
    out_dir = args[1]
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=args[0])
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    arm = next(o for o in scene.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
    mesh = next(o for o in scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    arm.name = "Armature"
    mesh.name = "SK_Publisher"
    to_centimetres(scene, arm, mesh)
    scene.render.fps = 30

    export(os.path.join(out_dir, MESH_FILE), [arm, mesh], False)
    print("[fbx] %s: %d bones, %d verts" % (MESH_FILE, len(arm.data.bones), len(mesh.data.vertices)))

    probe = {}
    for action in sorted(bpy.data.actions, key=lambda a: a.name):
        arm.animation_data.action = action
        arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
        first, last = (int(round(f)) for f in action.frame_range)
        scene.frame_start, scene.frame_end = first, last
        scene.name = action.name
        export(os.path.join(out_dir, action.name + ".fbx"), [arm], True)
        probe[action.name] = {"first": first, "last": last, "frames": {}}
        for frame in sorted({first, (first + last) // 2, last}):
            scene.frame_set(frame)
            probe[action.name]["frames"][str(frame)] = {
                pb.name: [round(c, 3) for c in (arm.matrix_world @ pb.head)] for pb in arm.pose.bones}
        print("[fbx] %s.fbx: frames %d..%d" % (action.name, first, last))
    if len(args) > 2:
        with open(args[2], "w") as out:
            json.dump(probe, out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
    bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="OBJECT")


def base_image(me):
    image = None
    for mat in me.materials:
        if mat and mat.use_nodes:
            for node in mat.node_tree.nodes:
                if node.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED":
                    link = node.inputs["Base Color"].links
                    if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                        image = link[0].from_node.image
    if image is None:
        image = next(i for i in bpy.data.images if i.size[0] > 0)
    return image


def vertex_colours(mesh):
    """Mean base-colour of each vertex, sampled through its UVs."""
    me = mesh.data
    image = base_image(me)
    w, h = image.size
    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    uv = np.zeros(len(me.loops) * 2, dtype=np.float32)
    me.uv_layers.active.data.foreach_get("uv", uv)
    uv = uv.reshape(-1, 2)
    vi = np.zeros(len(me.loops), dtype=np.int64)
    me.loops.foreach_get("vertex_index", vi)
    xs = np.clip((uv[:, 0] % 1.0 * w).astype(int), 0, w - 1)
    ys = np.clip((uv[:, 1] % 1.0 * h).astype(int), 0, h - 1)
    rgb = px[ys, xs, :3]
    total = np.zeros((len(me.vertices), 3))
    count = np.zeros(len(me.vertices))
    np.add.at(total, vi, rgb)
    np.add.at(count, vi, 1)
    return total / np.maximum(count, 1)[:, None]

"""

Renders a rigged character in the frames of its clips with the Workbench engine: textured, or coloured by the skin
weights (each bone its own colour, blended by weight), so bad deformation and its cause sit side by side.

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/render_poses.py -- <file.fbx|.glb|.blend> <out_dir>
        [--clips Idle,Slow_Orc_Walk] [--frames 6 | --at 1,20,40] [--views front,q3,side,back] [--mode texture|weights]
        [--size 512] [--rest] [--step 0] [--scale 3.6] [--focus neck_01]

Output: <out_dir>/<clip>_<view>_<frame:04d>.png. --rest renders the rest pose as clip "rest". --step N renders every
N-th frame of the clip instead of --frames (for a GIF). --focus centres the frame on a bone (with a small --scale: a
close-up).

import argparse
import colorsys
import math
import os
import sys

import bpy
from mathutils import Vector

VIEWS = {  # the character faces -Y
    "front": (0.0, -1.0), "q3": (-0.62, -0.78), "side": (-1.0, 0.0), "back": (0.0, 1.0), "q3b": (0.62, 0.78),
    "q3r": (0.62, -0.78),
}

    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("file")
    ap.add_argument("out")
    ap.add_argument("--clips", default="")

    ap.add_argument("--at", default="")

"""Probe the shirt under the Publisher's tie: which faces, which texels, and do they share texels with the tie strip.

blender -b --factory-startup --python probe_shirt.py -- <clips.blend> <out_no_tie.blend>
"""
import sys

import bmesh
import bpy
import numpy as np

args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=args[0])
mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
me = mesh.data
names = {g.index: g.name for g in mesh.vertex_groups}
tie_w = np.zeros(len(me.vertices))
for v in me.vertices:
    for g in v.groups:
        if names[g.group].startswith("tie_"):
            tie_w[v.index] += g.weight
co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
print("[probe] verts", len(co), "tie-weighted verts", int((tie_w > 0.5).sum()))
img = None
for n in me.materials[0].node_tree.nodes:
    if n.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
        print("[probe] image node", n.name, n.image.name, n.image.size[:], n.image.packed_file is not None,
              n.image.filepath)
uvl = me.uv_layers.active.data
tie_faces = [p for p in me.polygons if all(tie_w[v] > 0.5 for v in p.vertices)]
region = [p for p in me.polygons if not any(tie_w[v] > 0.5 for v in p.vertices)
          and all(abs(co[v][0]) < 0.14 and co[v][1] < -0.12 and 1.40 < co[v][2] < 2.20 for v in p.vertices)]
print("[probe] tie faces", len(tie_faces), "body faces in tie region", len(region))
tie_uv = {tuple(np.round(uvl[l].uv[:], 4)) for p in tie_faces for l in p.loop_indices}
shared = [p for p in region if all(tuple(np.round(uvl[l].uv[:], 4)) in tie_uv for l in p.loop_indices)]
print("[probe] region faces with UVs identical to tie UVs:", len(shared))
for p in shared[:5]:
    print("   face", p.index, [tuple(np.round(uvl[l].uv[:], 4)) for l in p.loop_indices],
          np.round(co[list(p.vertices)].mean(axis=0), 3))
# delete the tie strip and save for rendering
bm = bmesh.new()
bm.from_mesh(me)
bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=[bm.verts[i] for i in np.where(tie_w > 0.5)[0]], context="VERTS")
bm.to_mesh(me)
bm.free()
bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=args[1], copy=True)
print("[probe] saved", args[1])

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, repaints the base colour packed in a Publisher .blend).

Paints the shirt under the tie plain black. The tie was cut loose from the shirt (build_rig.py, split_tie), but the
shirt texels it was printed on still carry a grey imprint of it, which shows whenever the tie swings away. Every
texel of a shirt face in the chest box under the tie takes the plain black of the shirt around it. A texel that any
other face uses as well (the tie strip, the knot, the collar, the skin, the jacket) is left alone, and so is a face
whose UVs were folded onto one texel by build_rig.py (they point at the gold of the knot or at one black texel).

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/plain_shirt.py -- <file.blend> [--write] [report.txt]

Without --write it only measures. The report gives the shirt texels before and after.
"""
import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np

# The chest under the tie, in Blender metres (he faces -Y). Above TOP the knot and the collar begin.
BOX_X, BOX_Y, BOTTOM, TOP = 0.16, -0.12, 1.30, 2.12
# A texel of the shirt is plain if it is this close to the black of the shirt (largest channel difference).
PLAIN = 0.03


def base_image(me):
    for node in me.materials[0].node_tree.nodes:
        if node.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED":
            link = node.inputs["Base Color"].links
            if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                return link[0].from_node.image

import sys

import bmesh
import bpy

args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=args[0])
mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
me = mesh.data
names = {g.index: g.name for g in mesh.vertex_groups}
tie_w = np.zeros(len(me.vertices))
for v in me.vertices:
    for g in v.groups:
        if names[g.group].startswith("tie_"):
            tie_w[v.index] += g.weight
co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
print("[probe] verts", len(co), "tie-weighted verts", int((tie_w > 0.5).sum()))
img = None
for n in me.materials[0].node_tree.nodes:

uvl = me.uv_layers.active.data

region = [p for p in me.polygons if not any(tie_w[v] > 0.5 for v in p.vertices)

print("[probe] tie faces", len(tie_faces), "body faces in tie region", len(region))
tie_uv = {tuple(np.round(uvl[l].uv[:], 4)) for p in tie_faces for l in p.loop_indices}

print("[probe] region faces with UVs identical to tie UVs:", len(shared))

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, repaints the base colour packed in a Publisher .blend).

Paints the shirt under the tie plain black. The tie was cut loose from the shirt (build_rig.py, split_tie), but the
shirt texels it was printed on still carry a grey imprint of it, which shows whenever the tie swings away. Every
texel of a shirt face in the chest box under the tie takes the plain black of the shirt around it. A texel that any
other face uses as well (the tie strip, the knot, the collar, the skin, the jacket) is left alone, and so is a face
whose UVs were folded onto one texel by build_rig.py (they point at the gold of the knot or at one black texel).

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/plain_shirt.py -- <file.blend> [--write] [report.txt]

Without --write it only measures. The report gives the shirt texels before and after.
"""
import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np

# The chest under the tie, in Blender metres (he faces -Y). Above TOP the knot and the collar begin.
BOX_X, BOX_Y, BOTTOM, TOP = 0.16, -0.12, 1.30, 2.12
# A texel of the shirt is plain if it is this close to the black of the shirt (largest channel difference).
PLAIN = 0.03


def base_image(me):
    for node in me.materials[0].node_tree.nodes:
        if node.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED":
            link = node.inputs["Base Color"].links
            if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                return link[0].from_node.image
    raise RuntimeError("no base colour image")


def coverage(t, w, h):
    """Texels whose centre lies in a UV triangle given in texel units, plus a half-texel rim."""
    x0, y0 = np.floor(t.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
    x1, y1 = np.ceil(t.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
    d = (t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (t[0, 1] - t[2, 1])
    if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0 or abs(d) < 1e-9:
        return None
    xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
    b0 = ((t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    b1 = ((t[2, 1] - t[0, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    tol = min(0.5, 1.0 / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
    return slice(y0, y1 + 1), slice(x0, x1 + 1), (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (1 - b0 - b1 >= -tol)


def main():
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
    path, write = args[0], "--write" in args
    report = next((a for a in args[1:] if a != "--write"), None)
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    me = mesh.data
    image = base_image(me)
    w, h = image.size
    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    size = np.array((w, h))
    co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
    uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
    tie_groups = {g.index for g in mesh.vertex_groups if g.name.startswith("tie_")}
    on_tie = np.zeros(len(co), dtype=bool)
    for v in me.vertices:
        on_tie[v.index] = sum(g.weight for g in v.groups if g.group in tie_groups) > 0.5

    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    shirt = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    other = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    folded = 0
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        p = co[list(lt.vertices)]
        t = np.array([uv[l].uv[:] for l in lt.loops]) * size - 0.5
        cover = coverage(t, w, h)
        if cover is None or np.ptp(t, axis=0).max() < 0.5:
            folded += 1
            # A folded face still shows its one texel: keep it as it is.
            for x, y in t:
                other[min(max(int(round(y)), 0), h - 1), min(max(int(round(x)), 0), w - 1)] = True
            continue
        mine = (not on_tie[list(lt.vertices)].any() and np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < BOX_X)
                and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y) and np.all((p[:, 2] > BOTTOM) & (p[:, 2] < TOP)))
        (shirt if mine else other)[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
    region = shirt & ~other
    rgb = px[..., :3]
    # The plain black of the shirt: the median of the shirt texels that are already dark and grey-free.
    dark = region & (rgb.max(axis=-1) < 0.08)
    black = np.median(rgb[dark], axis=0)
    off = np.abs(rgb - black).max(axis=-1)
    before = rgb[region]
    lines = [
        "%s" % path,
        "shirt texels under the tie: %d (%d shared with other faces and left alone), %d folded faces skipped"
        % (region.sum(), (shirt & other).sum(), folded),
        "black of the shirt: %s" % np.round(black, 4).tolist(),
        "before: mean %s, max value %.3f, texels off the black by > %.2f: %d"
        % (np.round(before.mean(axis=0), 4).tolist(), before.max(), PLAIN, int((off[region] > PLAIN).sum())),
    ]
    if write:
        rgb[region] = black
        image.pixels.foreach_set(px.ravel())
        image.update()
        image.pack()
        after = px[..., :3][region]
        off = np.abs(px[..., :3] - black).max(axis=-1)
        lines.append("after:  mean %s, max value %.3f, texels off the black by > %.2f: %d"
                     % (np.round(after.mean(axis=0), 4).tolist(), after.max(), PLAIN, int((off[region] > PLAIN).sum())))
        bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()
        lines.append("saved")
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    print("\n".join("[shirt] " + l for l in lines))
    if report:
        with open(report, "w") as out:
            out.write(text + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, repaints the textures packed in a Publisher .blend).

Paints the shirt under the tie plain black. When the tie was cut loose (build_rig.py, split_tie) the shirt under it
kept a tie-shaped patch: its faces were folded onto one texel of the chest, slightly grey, warm and with a tilted
normal, so it shows as a grey imprint of the tie whenever the tie swings away. This tool

- paints a square of texels around that texel with the black, the normal and the roughness of the shirt beside the
  tie (medians), as far as every texel in the square belongs to dark shirt faces only;
- paints the grey texels of the unfolded shirt faces under the tie black, never a texel that any other face (the tie
  strip, the knot, the collar, the skin, the jacket) uses, nor a coloured one (the gold of the knot).

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/plain_shirt.py -- <file.blend> [--write] [report.txt]

Without --write it only measures. The report gives the shirt texels before and after.
"""
import sys
from collections import Counter

import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import kdtree

# The chest under the tie, in Blender metres (he faces -Y). Above TOP the knot and the collar begin.
BOX_X, BOX_Y, BOTTOM, TOP = 0.16, -0.12, 1.30, 2.12
# A shirt face is under the tie if its centre lies this close (m) to a vert of the tie strip.
MARGIN = 0.04
# The shirt beside the tie that gives the black: |x| from, |x| to, z from, z to.
SIDE = (0.16, 0.26, 1.55, 2.00)
# A texel is off the black if a channel differs by more than this; grey if its channels differ by less than GREY.
PLAIN, GREY = 0.012, 0.05
# Half size (texels) of the square painted around the folded texel, at most: mip levels see this far.
SPOT = 8


def images(me):
    """The four textures of the material by their input on the shader."""
    found = {}
    for node in me.materials[0].node_tree.nodes:
        if node.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED":
            for name, socket in (("base", "Base Color"), ("rough", "Roughness"), ("metal", "Metallic")):
                link = node.inputs[socket].links
                if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                    found[name] = link[0].from_node.image
        if node.type == "NORMAL_MAP":
            link = node.inputs["Color"].links
            if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                found["normal"] = link[0].from_node.image
    if set(found) != {"base", "rough", "metal", "normal"}:
        raise RuntimeError("textures found: %s" % sorted(found))
    return found


def coverage(t, w, h):
    """Texels whose centre lies in a UV triangle given in texel units, plus a half-texel rim."""
    x0, y0 = np.floor(t.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
    x1, y1 = np.ceil(t.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
    d = (t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (t[0, 1] - t[2, 1])
    if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0 or abs(d) < 1e-9:
        return None
    xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
    b0 = ((t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    b1 = ((t[2, 1] - t[0, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    tol = min(0.5, 1.0 / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))

    part = rgb[mask]
    off = np.abs(part - black).max(axis=-1)
    return "%d texels, mean %s, brightest %.3f, off the black by > %.3f: %d" % (
        len(part), np.round(part.mean(axis=0), 4).tolist(), part.max(), PLAIN, int((off > PLAIN).sum()))


def main():
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
    path, write = args[0], "--write" in args
    report = next((a for a in args[1:] if a != "--write"), None)
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    me = mesh.data
    maps = images(me)
    w, h = maps["base"].size
    px = {k: np.array(im.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4) for k, im in maps.items()}
    size = np.array((w, h))

    uv = me.uv_layers.active.data

    strip = kdtree.KDTree(int(on_tie.sum()))
    for k, i in enumerate(np.where(on_tie)[0]):
        strip.insert(co[i], k)
    strip.balance()
    base = px["base"][..., :3]

    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    shirt = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # unfolded shirt faces under the tie
    beside = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)  # shirt faces beside the tie
    other = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # every other face
    spots = Counter()
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        p = co[list(lt.vertices)]
        t = np.array([uv[l].uv[:] for l in lt.loops]) * size - 0.5
        body = not on_tie[list(lt.vertices)].any()
        under = (body and np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < BOX_X) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                 and np.all((p[:, 2] > BOTTOM) & (p[:, 2] < TOP)) and strip.find(p.mean(axis=0))[2] < MARGIN)
        cover = coverage(t, w, h)
        if cover is None or np.ptp(t, axis=0).max() < 0.5:
            x, y = (min(max(int(round(c)), 0), n - 1) for c, n in zip(t.mean(axis=0), (w, h)))

        side = (body and np.all((np.abs(p[:, 0]) > SIDE[0]) & (np.abs(p[:, 0]) < SIDE[1])) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                and np.all((p[:, 2] > SIDE[2]) & (p[:, 2] < SIDE[3])))

    black = look["base"]
    lines = ["%s" % path, "shirt beside the tie, %d texels (spread %.4f): %s" % (
        dark.sum(), base[dark].std(axis=0).max(),
        ", ".join("%s %s" % (k, np.round(v, 3).tolist()) for k, v in look.items()))]

    paint = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    for (y, x), n in spots.most_common():
        c = base[y, x]
        if c.max() - c.min() > GREY:
            lines.append("folded spot (%d, %d), %d faces: coloured %s, left alone" % (x, y, n, np.round(c, 3).tolist()))
            continue

        r = 0
        while r < SPOT:
            q = (slice(max(y - r - 1, 0), y + r + 2), slice(max(x - r - 1, 0), x + r + 2))
            used = other[q] | shirt[q]
            if (used & (base[q].max(axis=-1) > 0.15)).any() or (used & ~(beside[q] | shirt[q]) & ~dark[q]).any():

        lines.append("folded spot (%d, %d), %d faces: base %s normal %s rough %.3f, square of %d texels" % (
            x, y, n, np.round(c, 3).tolist(), np.round(px["normal"][y, x, :3], 3).tolist(), px["rough"][y, x, 0],
            (2 * r + 1) ** 2))
    grey = shirt & ~other & (base.max(axis=-1) - base.min(axis=-1) < GREY) & (base.max(axis=-1) < 0.5)
    paint_grey = grey & (np.abs(base - black).max(axis=-1) > PLAIN)
    lines.append("unfolded shirt under the tie: %d texels (%d shared with other faces), %d grey off the black" % (
        (shirt & ~other).sum(), (shirt & other).sum(), paint_grey.sum()))
    every = paint | paint_grey
    lines.append("before: " + stats(base, every, black))
    if write:
        base[every] = black
        px["normal"][..., :3][paint] = look["normal"]
        px["rough"][..., :3][paint] = look["rough"]
        for k, im in maps.items():
            im.pixels.foreach_set(px[k].ravel())
            im.update()
            im.pack()
        lines.append("after:  " + stats(base, every, black))
        bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()
        lines.append("saved")
    print("\n".join("[shirt] " + l for l in lines))
    if report:
        with open(report, "w") as out:
            out.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

                link = node.inputs[socket].links
                if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                    found[name] = link[0].from_node.image
        if node.type == "NORMAL_MAP":
            link = node.inputs["Color"].links
            if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                found["normal"] = link[0].from_node.image
    if set(found) != {"base", "rough", "metal", "normal"}:
        raise RuntimeError("textures found: %s" % sorted(found))
    return found


def coverage(t, w, h):
    """Texels whose centre lies in a UV triangle given in texel units, plus a half-texel rim."""
    x0, y0 = np.floor(t.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
    x1, y1 = np.ceil(t.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
    d = (t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (t[0, 1] - t[2, 1])
    if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0 or abs(d) < 1e-9:
        return None
    xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
    b0 = ((t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    b1 = ((t[2, 1] - t[0, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    tol = min(0.5, 1.0 / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
    return slice(y0, y1 + 1), slice(x0, x1 + 1), (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (1 - b0 - b1 >= -tol)


def stats(rgb, mask, black):
    part = rgb[mask]
    off = np.abs(part - black).max(axis=-1)
    return "%d texels, mean %s, brightest %.3f, off the black by > %.3f: %d" % (
        len(part), np.round(part.mean(axis=0), 4).tolist(), part.max(), PLAIN, int((off > PLAIN).sum()))


def main():
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
    path, write = args[0], "--write" in args
    report = next((a for a in args[1:] if a != "--write"), None)
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    me = mesh.data
    maps = images(me)
    w, h = maps["base"].size
    px = {k: np.array(im.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4) for k, im in maps.items()}
    size = np.array((w, h))
    co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
    uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
    tie_groups = {g.index for g in mesh.vertex_groups if g.name.startswith("tie_")}
    on_tie = np.array([sum(g.weight for g in v.groups if g.group in tie_groups) > 0.5 for v in me.vertices])
    strip = kdtree.KDTree(int(on_tie.sum()))
    for k, i in enumerate(np.where(on_tie)[0]):
        strip.insert(co[i], k)
    strip.balance()
    base = px["base"][..., :3]

    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    shirt = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # unfolded shirt faces under the tie
    beside = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)  # shirt faces beside the tie
    other = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # every other face
    spots = Counter()
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        p = co[list(lt.vertices)]
        t = np.array([uv[l].uv[:] for l in lt.loops]) * size - 0.5
        body = not on_tie[list(lt.vertices)].any()
        under = (body and np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < BOX_X) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                 and np.all((p[:, 2] > BOTTOM) & (p[:, 2] < TOP)) and strip.find(p.mean(axis=0))[2] < MARGIN)
        cover = coverage(t, w, h)
        if cover is None or np.ptp(t, axis=0).max() < 0.5:
            x, y = (min(max(int(round(c)), 0), n - 1) for c, n in zip(t.mean(axis=0), (w, h)))
            if under:
                spots[(y, x)] += 1
            else:
                other[y, x] = True
            continue
        (shirt if under else other)[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
        side = (body and np.all((np.abs(p[:, 0]) > SIDE[0]) & (np.abs(p[:, 0]) < SIDE[1])) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                and np.all((p[:, 2] > SIDE[2]) & (p[:, 2] < SIDE[3])))
        if side:
            beside[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]

    # The shirt beside the tie: its black, normal and roughness.
    dark = beside & ~shirt & (base.max(axis=-1) < 0.15)
    look = {k: np.median(px[k][..., :3][dark], axis=0) for k in ("base", "normal", "rough", "metal")}
    black = look["base"]
    lines = ["%s" % path, "shirt beside the tie, %d texels (spread %.4f): %s" % (
        dark.sum(), base[dark].std(axis=0).max(),
        ", ".join("%s %s" % (k, np.round(v, 3).tolist()) for k, v in look.items()))]

    # The texels the folded faces under the tie point at; a gold one belongs to the knot and stays.
    paint = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    for (y, x), n in spots.most_common():
        c = base[y, x]
        if c.max() - c.min() > GREY:
            lines.append("folded spot (%d, %d), %d faces: coloured %s, left alone" % (x, y, n, np.round(c, 3).tolist()))
            continue
        # The square grows while every texel in it is used by dark shirt faces only, or by none.
        r = 0
        while r < SPOT:
            q = (slice(max(y - r - 1, 0), y + r + 2), slice(max(x - r - 1, 0), x + r + 2))
            used = other[q] | shirt[q]
            if (used & (base[q].max(axis=-1) > 0.15)).any() or (used & ~(beside[q] | shirt[q]) & ~dark[q]).any():
                break
            r += 1
        paint[max(y - r, 0):y + r + 1, max(x - r, 0):x + r + 1] = True
        lines.append("folded spot (%d, %d), %d faces: base %s normal %s rough %.3f, square of %d texels" % (
            x, y, n, np.round(c, 3).tolist(), np.round(px["normal"][y, x, :3], 3).tolist(), px["rough"][y, x, 0],
            (2 * r + 1) ** 2))
    grey = shirt & ~other & (base.max(axis=-1) - base.min(axis=-1) < GREY) & (base.max(axis=-1) < 0.5)
    paint_grey = grey & (np.abs(base - black).max(axis=-1) > PLAIN)
    lines.append("unfolded shirt under the tie: %d texels (%d shared with other faces), %d grey off the black" % (
        (shirt & ~other).sum(), (shirt & other).sum(), paint_grey.sum()))
    every = paint | paint_grey
    lines.append("before: " + stats(base, every, black))
    if write:
        base[every] = black
        px["normal"][..., :3][paint] = look["normal"]
        px["rough"][..., :3][paint] = look["rough"]
        for k, im in maps.items():
            im.pixels.foreach_set(px[k].ravel())
            im.update()
            im.pack()
        lines.append("after:  " + stats(base, every, black))
        bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()
        lines.append("saved")
    print("\n".join("[shirt] " + l for l in lines))
    if report:
        with open(report, "w") as out:
            out.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, repaints the base colour packed in a Publisher .blend).

Paints the shirt under the tie plain black. The tie was cut loose from the shirt (build_rig.py, split_tie), but the
shirt texels it was printed on still carry a grey imprint of it, which shows whenever the tie swings away. Every
texel of a shirt face in the chest box under the tie takes the plain black of the shirt around it. A texel that any
other face uses as well (the tie strip, the knot, the collar, the skin, the jacket) is left alone, and so is a face
whose UVs were folded onto one texel by build_rig.py (they point at the gold of the knot or at one black texel).

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/plain_shirt.py -- <file.blend> [--write] [report.txt]

Without --write it only measures. The report gives the shirt texels before and after.
"""
import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import kdtree

# The chest under the tie, in Blender metres (he faces -Y). Above TOP the knot and the collar begin.
BOX_X, BOX_Y, BOTTOM, TOP = 0.16, -0.12, 1.30, 2.12
# A shirt face is under the tie if its centre lies this close (m) to a vert of the tie strip.
MARGIN = 0.04
# The shirt beside the tie that gives the black: |x| from, |x| to, z from, z to.
SIDE = (0.16, 0.26, 1.55, 2.00)
# A texel of the shirt is plain if it is this close to the black of the shirt (largest channel difference).
PLAIN = 0.03


def base_image(me):
    for node in me.materials[0].node_tree.nodes:
        if node.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED":
            link = node.inputs["Base Color"].links
            if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                return link[0].from_node.image
    raise RuntimeError("no base colour image")


def coverage(t, w, h):
    """Texels whose centre lies in a UV triangle given in texel units, plus a half-texel rim."""
    x0, y0 = np.floor(t.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
    x1, y1 = np.ceil(t.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
    d = (t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (t[0, 1] - t[2, 1])
    if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0 or abs(d) < 1e-9:
        return None
    xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
    b0 = ((t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    b1 = ((t[2, 1] - t[0, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    tol = min(0.5, 1.0 / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
    return slice(y0, y1 + 1), slice(x0, x1 + 1), (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (1 - b0 - b1 >= -tol)


def main():
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
    path, write = args[0], "--write" in args
    report = next((a for a in args[1:] if a != "--write"), None)
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    me = mesh.data
    image = base_image(me)
    w, h = image.size
    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    size = np.array((w, h))
    co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
    uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
    tie_groups = {g.index for g in mesh.vertex_groups if g.name.startswith("tie_")}
    on_tie = np.zeros(len(co), dtype=bool)
    for v in me.vertices:
        on_tie[v.index] = sum(g.weight for g in v.groups if g.group in tie_groups) > 0.5

    strip = kdtree.KDTree(int(on_tie.sum()))
    for k, i in enumerate(np.where(on_tie)[0]):
        strip.insert(co[i], k)
    strip.balance()

    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    shirt = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    beside = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    other = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    folded = 0
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        p = co[list(lt.vertices)]
        t = np.array([uv[l].uv[:] for l in lt.loops]) * size - 0.5
        cover = coverage(t, w, h)
        if cover is None or np.ptp(t, axis=0).max() < 0.5:
            folded += 1
            # A folded face still shows its one texel: keep it as it is.
            for x, y in t:
                other[min(max(int(round(y)), 0), h - 1), min(max(int(round(x)), 0), w - 1)] = True
            continue
        body = not on_tie[list(lt.vertices)].any()
        in_box = (np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < BOX_X) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                  and np.all((p[:, 2] > BOTTOM) & (p[:, 2] < TOP)))
        mine = body and in_box and strip.find(p.mean(axis=0))[2] < MARGIN
        side = (body and np.all((np.abs(p[:, 0]) > SIDE[0]) & (np.abs(p[:, 0]) < SIDE[1])) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                and np.all((p[:, 2] > SIDE[2]) & (p[:, 2] < SIDE[3])))
        (shirt if mine else other)[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
        if side:
            beside[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
    region = shirt & ~other
    rgb = px[..., :3]
    # The plain black of the shirt: the median of the dark shirt texels beside the tie (the jacket there is bright).
    dark = beside & ~shirt & (rgb.max(axis=-1) < 0.15)
    black = np.median(rgb[dark], axis=0)
    off = np.abs(rgb - black).max(axis=-1)
    before = rgb[region]
    lines = [
        "%s" % path,
        "shirt texels under the tie: %d (%d shared with other faces and left alone), %d folded faces skipped"
        % (region.sum(), (shirt & other).sum(), folded),
        "black of the shirt: %s from %d texels beside the tie (spread %.4f)"
        % (np.round(black, 4).tolist(), dark.sum(), rgb[dark].std(axis=0).max()),
        "before: mean %s, max value %.3f, texels off the black by > %.2f: %d"
        % (np.round(before.mean(axis=0), 4).tolist(), before.max(), PLAIN, int((off[region] > PLAIN).sum())),
    ]
    if write:
        rgb[region] = black
        image.pixels.foreach_set(px.ravel())
        image.update()
        image.pack()
        after = px[..., :3][region]
        off = np.abs(px[..., :3] - black).max(axis=-1)
        lines.append("after:  mean %s, max value %.3f, texels off the black by > %.2f: %d"
                     % (np.round(after.mean(axis=0), 4).tolist(), after.max(), PLAIN, int((off[region] > PLAIN).sum())))
        bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()
        lines.append("saved")
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    print("\n".join("[shirt] " + l for l in lines))
    if report:
        with open(report, "w") as out:
            out.write(text + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, repaints the textures packed in a Publisher .blend).

Paints the shirt under the tie plain black. When the tie was cut loose (build_rig.py, split_tie) the shirt under it
kept a tie-shaped patch: its faces were folded onto one texel of the chest, slightly grey, warm and with a tilted
normal, so it shows as a grey imprint of the tie whenever the tie swings away. This tool

- paints a square of texels around that texel with the black, the normal and the roughness of the shirt beside the
  tie (medians), as far as every texel in the square belongs to dark shirt faces only;
- paints the grey texels of the unfolded shirt faces under the tie black, never a texel that any other face (the tie
  strip, the knot, the collar, the skin, the jacket) uses, nor a coloured one (the gold of the knot).

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/plain_shirt.py -- <file.blend> [--write] [report.txt]

Without --write it only measures. The report gives the shirt texels before and after.
"""
import sys
from collections import Counter

import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import kdtree

# The chest under the tie, in Blender metres (he faces -Y). Above TOP the knot and the collar begin.
BOX_X, BOX_Y, BOTTOM, TOP = 0.16, -0.12, 1.30, 2.12
# A shirt face is under the tie if its centre lies this close (m) to a vert of the tie strip.
MARGIN = 0.04
# The shirt beside the tie that gives the black: |x| from, |x| to, z from, z to.
SIDE = (0.16, 0.26, 1.55, 2.00)
# A texel is off the black if a channel differs by more than this; grey if its channels differ by less than GREY.
PLAIN, GREY = 0.012, 0.05
# Half size (texels) of the square painted around the folded texel, at most: mip levels see this far.
SPOT = 8


def images(me):
    """The four textures of the material by their input on the shader."""
    found = {}
    for node in me.materials[0].node_tree.nodes:
        if node.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED":
            for name, socket in (("base", "Base Color"), ("rough", "Roughness"), ("metal", "Metallic")):
                link = node.inputs[socket].links
                if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                    found[name] = link[0].from_node.image
        if node.type == "NORMAL_MAP":
            link = node.inputs["Color"].links
            if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                found["normal"] = link[0].from_node.image
    if set(found) != {"base", "rough", "metal", "normal"}:
        raise RuntimeError("textures found: %s" % sorted(found))
    return found


def coverage(t, w, h):
    """Texels whose centre lies in a UV triangle given in texel units, plus a half-texel rim."""
    x0, y0 = np.floor(t.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
    x1, y1 = np.ceil(t.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
    d = (t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (t[0, 1] - t[2, 1])
    if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0 or abs(d) < 1e-9:
        return None
    xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
    b0 = ((t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    b1 = ((t[2, 1] - t[0, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    tol = min(0.5, 1.0 / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
    return slice(y0, y1 + 1), slice(x0, x1 + 1), (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (1 - b0 - b1 >= -tol)


def stats(rgb, mask, black):
    part = rgb[mask]
    off = np.abs(part - black).max(axis=-1)
    return "%d texels, mean %s, brightest %.3f, off the black by > %.3f: %d" % (
        len(part), np.round(part.mean(axis=0), 4).tolist(), part.max(), PLAIN, int((off > PLAIN).sum()))


def main():
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
    path, write = args[0], "--write" in args
    report = next((a for a in args[1:] if a != "--write"), None)
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    me = mesh.data
    maps = images(me)
    w, h = maps["base"].size
    px = {k: np.array(im.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4) for k, im in maps.items()}
    size = np.array((w, h))
    co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
    uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
    tie_groups = {g.index for g in mesh.vertex_groups if g.name.startswith("tie_")}
    on_tie = np.array([sum(g.weight for g in v.groups if g.group in tie_groups) > 0.5 for v in me.vertices])
    strip = kdtree.KDTree(int(on_tie.sum()))
    for k, i in enumerate(np.where(on_tie)[0]):
        strip.insert(co[i], k)
    strip.balance()
    base = px["base"][..., :3]

    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    shirt = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # unfolded shirt faces under the tie
    beside = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)  # shirt faces beside the tie
    other = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # every other face
    spots = Counter()
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        p = co[list(lt.vertices)]
        t = np.array([uv[l].uv[:] for l in lt.loops]) * size - 0.5
        body = not on_tie[list(lt.vertices)].any()
        under = (body and np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < BOX_X) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                 and np.all((p[:, 2] > BOTTOM) & (p[:, 2] < TOP)) and strip.find(p.mean(axis=0))[2] < MARGIN)
        cover = coverage(t, w, h)
        if cover is None or np.ptp(t, axis=0).max() < 0.5:
            x, y = (min(max(int(round(c)), 0), n - 1) for c, n in zip(t.mean(axis=0), (w, h)))
            if under:
                spots[(y, x)] += 1
            else:
                other[y, x] = True
            continue
        (shirt if under else other)[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
        side = (body and np.all((np.abs(p[:, 0]) > SIDE[0]) & (np.abs(p[:, 0]) < SIDE[1])) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                and np.all((p[:, 2] > SIDE[2]) & (p[:, 2] < SIDE[3])))
        if side:
            beside[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]

    # The shirt beside the tie: its black, normal and roughness.
    dark = beside & ~shirt & (base.max(axis=-1) < 0.15)
    look = {k: np.median(px[k][..., :3][dark], axis=0) for k in ("base", "normal", "rough", "metal")}
    black = look["base"]
    lines = ["%s" % path, "shirt beside the tie, %d texels (spread %.4f): %s" % (
        dark.sum(), base[dark].std(axis=0).max(),
        ", ".join("%s %s" % (k, np.round(v, 3).tolist()) for k, v in look.items()))]

    # The texels the folded faces under the tie point at; a gold one belongs to the knot and stays.
    paint = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    for (y, x), n in spots.most_common():
        c = base[y, x]
        if c.max() - c.min() > GREY:
            lines.append("folded spot (%d, %d), %d faces: coloured %s, left alone" % (x, y, n, np.round(c, 3).tolist()))
            continue
        # The square grows while every texel in it is used by dark shirt faces only, or by none.
        r = 0
        while r < SPOT:
            q = (slice(max(y - r - 1, 0), y + r + 2), slice(max(x - r - 1, 0), x + r + 2))
            used = other[q] | shirt[q]
            if (used & (base[q].max(axis=-1) > 0.15)).any() or (used & ~(beside[q] | shirt[q]) & ~dark[q]).any():
                break
            r += 1
        paint[max(y - r, 0):y + r + 1, max(x - r, 0):x + r + 1] = True
        lines.append("folded spot (%d, %d), %d faces: base %s normal %s rough %.3f, square of %d texels" % (
            x, y, n, np.round(c, 3).tolist(), np.round(px["normal"][y, x, :3], 3).tolist(), px["rough"][y, x, 0],
            (2 * r + 1) ** 2))
    grey = shirt & ~other & (base.max(axis=-1) - base.min(axis=-1) < GREY) & (base.max(axis=-1) < 0.5)
    paint_grey = grey & (np.abs(base - black).max(axis=-1) > PLAIN)
    lines.append("unfolded shirt under the tie: %d texels (%d shared with other faces), %d grey off the black" % (
        (shirt & ~other).sum(), (shirt & other).sum(), paint_grey.sum()))
    every = paint | paint_grey
    lines.append("before: " + stats(base, every, black))
    if write:
        base[every] = black
        px["normal"][..., :3][paint] = look["normal"]
        px["rough"][..., :3][paint] = look["rough"]
        for k, im in maps.items():
            im.pixels.foreach_set(px[k].ravel())
            im.update()
            im.pack()
        lines.append("after:  " + stats(base, every, black))
        bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()
        lines.append("saved")
    print("\n".join("[shirt] " + l for l in lines))
    if report:
        with open(report, "w") as out:
            out.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
