    d = (t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (t[0, 1] - t[2, 1])
    if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0 or abs(d) < 1e-9:
        return None
    xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
    b0 = ((t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    b1 = ((t[2, 1] - t[0, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    tol = min(0.5, 1.0 / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
    return slice(y0, y1 + 1), slice(x0, x1 + 1), (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (1 - b0 - b1 >= -tol)


def stats(rgb, mask, black):
    part = rgb[mask]
    off = np.abs(part - black).max(axis=-1)
    return "%d texels, mean %s, brightest %.3f, off the black by > %.3f: %d" % (
        len(part), np.round(part.mean(axis=0), 4).tolist(), part.max(), PLAIN, int((off > PLAIN).sum()))


def main():
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
    path, write = args[0], "--write" in args
    report = next((a for a in args[1:] if a != "--write"), None)
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    me = mesh.data
    maps = images(me)
    w, h = maps["base"].size
    px = {k: np.array(im.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4) for k, im in maps.items()}
    size = np.array((w, h))
    co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
    uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
    tie_groups = {g.index for g in mesh.vertex_groups if g.name.startswith("tie_")}
    on_tie = np.array([sum(g.weight for g in v.groups if g.group in tie_groups) > 0.5 for v in me.vertices])
    strip = kdtree.KDTree(int(on_tie.sum()))
    for k, i in enumerate(np.where(on_tie)[0]):
        strip.insert(co[i], k)
    strip.balance()
    base = px["base"][..., :3]

    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    shirt = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # unfolded shirt faces under the tie
    beside = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)  # shirt faces beside the tie
    other = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # every other face
    foreign = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)  # faces off the front of the chest
    spots = Counter()
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        p = co[list(lt.vertices)]
        t = np.array([uv[l].uv[:] for l in lt.loops]) * size - 0.5
        body = not on_tie[list(lt.vertices)].any()
        under = (body and np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < BOX_X) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                 and np.all((p[:, 2] > BOTTOM) & (p[:, 2] < TOP)) and strip.find(p.mean(axis=0))[2] < MARGIN)
        front = (body and np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < CHEST_X) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                 and np.all((p[:, 2] > BOTTOM) & (p[:, 2] < TOP)))
        cover = coverage(t, w, h)
        if cover is None or np.ptp(t, axis=0).max() < 0.5:
            x, y = (min(max(int(round(c)), 0), n - 1) for c, n in zip(t.mean(axis=0), (w, h)))
            if under:
                spots[(y, x)] += 1
            else:
                other[y, x] = True
                foreign[y, x] |= not front
            continue
        (shirt if under else other)[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
        if not front:
            foreign[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
        side = (body and np.all((np.abs(p[:, 0]) > SIDE[0]) & (np.abs(p[:, 0]) < SIDE[1])) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                and np.all((p[:, 2] > SIDE[2]) & (p[:, 2] < SIDE[3])))
        if side:
            beside[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]

    # The shirt beside the tie: its black, normal and roughness.
    dark = beside & ~shirt & (base.max(axis=-1) < 0.15)
    look = {k: np.median(px[k][..., :3][dark], axis=0) for k in ("base", "normal", "rough", "metal")}
    black = look["base"]
    lines = ["%s" % path, "shirt beside the tie, %d texels (spread %.4f): %s" % (
        dark.sum(), base[dark].std(axis=0).max(),
        ", ".join("%s %s" % (k, np.round(v, 3).tolist()) for k, v in look.items()))]

    # The texels the folded faces under the tie point at; a gold one belongs to the knot and stays.
    paint = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    for (y, x), n in spots.most_common():
        c = base[y, x]
        if c.max() - c.min() > GREY:
            lines.append("folded spot (%d, %d), %d faces: coloured %s, left alone" % (x, y, n, np.round(c, 3).tolist()))
            continue
        # The square grows while every texel in it is dark and used by faces of the front of the chest only, or by
        # none: no tie, no knot, no collar, no skin, no jacket.
        r = 0
        while r < SPOT:
            q = (slice(max(y - r - 1, 0), y + r + 2), slice(max(x - r - 1, 0), x + r + 2))
            used = other[q] | shirt[q]
            if (used & (base[q].max(axis=-1) > 0.15)).any() or foreign[q].any():
                break
            r += 1
        paint[max(y - r, 0):y + r + 1, max(x - r, 0):x + r + 1] = True
        lines.append("folded spot (%d, %d), %d faces: base %s normal %s rough %.3f, square of %d texels" % (
            x, y, n, np.round(c, 3).tolist(), np.round(px["normal"][y, x, :3], 3).tolist(), px["rough"][y, x, 0],
            (2 * r + 1) ** 2))
    grey = shirt & ~other & (base.max(axis=-1) - base.min(axis=-1) < GREY) & (base.max(axis=-1) < 0.5)
    paint_grey = grey & (np.abs(base - black).max(axis=-1) > PLAIN)
    lines.append("unfolded shirt under the tie: %d texels (%d shared with other faces), %d grey off the black" % (
        (shirt & ~other).sum(), (shirt & other).sum(), paint_grey.sum()))
    every = paint | paint_grey
    lines.append("before: " + stats(base, every, black))
    if write:
        base[every] = black
        px["normal"][..., :3][paint] = look["normal"]
        px["rough"][..., :3][paint] = look["rough"]
        for k, im in maps.items():
            im.pixels.foreach_set(px[k].ravel())
            im.update()
            im.pack()
        lines.append("after:  " + stats(base, every, black))
        bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()
        lines.append("saved")
    print("\n".join("[shirt] " + l for l in lines))
    if report:
        with open(report, "w") as out:
            out.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, changes the UVs and the base colour of a Publisher .blend).

Makes the shirt under the tie plain black. When the tie was cut loose (build_rig.py, split_tie) the shirt faces it
lay on were folded onto one texel of "plain black" (plain_black_uv). That texel lies on a black sliver two or three
texels wide between texels of the cream jacket, so as soon as the texture is seen at a lower mip level the whole
tie-shaped patch takes the average of the two and shows as a grey imprint of the tie. This tool

- moves the UVs of those folded faces to the centre of the widest square of plain shirt in the texture (base colour
  at the black of the shirt beside the tie, a flat normal, the shirt's roughness, no metal, used by shirt faces of the
  front of the chest only), so every mip level sees black there. No texel changes for this;
- paints the grey texels of the unfolded shirt faces under the tie black, never a texel that any other face (the tie
  strip, the knot, the collar, the skin, the jacket) uses, nor a coloured one (the gold of the knot).

Folded faces outside the chest under the tie (the collar of neck_border, the gold under the knot) are left alone.

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/plain_shirt.py -- <file.blend> [--write] [report.txt]

Without --write it only measures. The report compares the colour the shirt under the tie shows before and after, at
full size and averaged over squares of 4 to 32 texels (what the lower mip levels see).
"""
import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import kdtree

# The chest under the tie, in Blender metres (he faces -Y). Above TOP the knot and the collar begin.
BOX_X, BOX_Y, BOTTOM, TOP = 0.16, -0.12, 1.30, 2.12
# A shirt face is under the tie if its centre lies this close (m) to a vert of the tie strip.
MARGIN = 0.04
# The shirt beside the tie that gives the black: |x| from, |x| to, z from, z to.
SIDE = (0.16, 0.26, 1.55, 2.00)
# The front of the chest between the lapels: the new spot is used by faces of it only.
CHEST_X = 0.40
# A texel is off the shirt if a channel of a map differs by more than this from the shirt beside the tie.
PLAIN = {"base": 0.012, "normal": 0.03, "rough": 0.05, "metal": 0.05}
# A texel is grey (not the gold of the knot) if its channels differ by less than this.
GREY = 0.05
# Half sizes of the squares averaged in the report, like mip levels 2 to 5.
MIPS = (2, 4, 8, 16)


def images(me):
    """The four textures of the material by their input on the shader."""
    found = {}
    for node in me.materials[0].node_tree.nodes:
        if node.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED":
            for name, socket in (("base", "Base Color"), ("rough", "Roughness"), ("metal", "Metallic")):
                link = node.inputs[socket].links
                if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                    found[name] = link[0].from_node.image
        if node.type == "NORMAL_MAP":
            link = node.inputs["Color"].links
            if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                found["normal"] = link[0].from_node.image
    if set(found) != {"base", "rough", "metal", "normal"}:
        raise RuntimeError("textures found: %s" % sorted(found))
    return found


def coverage(t, w, h):
    """Texels whose centre lies in a UV triangle given in texel units, plus a half-texel rim."""
    x0, y0 = np.floor(t.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
    x1, y1 = np.ceil(t.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
    d = (t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (t[0, 1] - t[2, 1])
    if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0 or abs(d) < 1e-9:
        return None
    xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
    b0 = ((t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    b1 = ((t[2, 1] - t[0, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    tol = min(0.5, 1.0 / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
    return slice(y0, y1 + 1), slice(x0, x1 + 1), (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (1 - b0 - b1 >= -tol)


def widest_square(ok):
    """Centre (y, x) and half size of the largest square of True texels."""
    h, w = ok.shape
    run = np.zeros((h + 1, w + 1), dtype=np.int32)
    best, where = 0, (0, 0)
    for y in range(h):
        row = ok[y]
        for x in np.where(row)[0]:
            run[y + 1, x + 1] = 1 + min(run[y, x], run[y, x + 1], run[y + 1, x])
        k = int(run[y + 1].max())
        if k > best:
            best = k
            x = int(run[y + 1].argmax()) - 1
            where = (y - k // 2, x - k // 2)
    return where, (best - 1) // 2


def shown(base, faces, size):
    """Mean colour the faces show: per face the texels under it, or for a folded face its one texel, with the
    average over the squares of MIPS around the place it samples."""
    h, w = base.shape[:2]
    full, mips = [], {r: [] for r in MIPS}
    for t in faces:
        x, y = (min(max(int(round(c)), 0), n - 1) for c, n in zip((t * size - 0.5).mean(axis=0), (w, h)))
        full.append(base[y, x])
        for r in MIPS:
            mips[r].append(base[max(y - r, 0):y + r, max(x - r, 0):x + r].reshape(-1, 3).mean(axis=0))
    out = ["full %s" % np.round(np.mean(full, axis=0), 3).tolist()]
    out += ["%dx%d %s" % (2 * r, 2 * r, np.round(np.mean(mips[r], axis=0), 3).tolist()) for r in MIPS]
    return ", ".join(out)


def main():
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
    path, write = args[0], "--write" in args
    report = next((a for a in args[1:] if a != "--write"), None)
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    me = mesh.data
    maps = images(me)
    w, h = maps["base"].size
    px = {k: np.array(im.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)[..., :3] for k, im in maps.items()}
    base = px["base"]
    size = np.array((w, h))
    co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
    uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
    tie_groups = {g.index for g in mesh.vertex_groups if g.name.startswith("tie_")}
    on_tie = np.array([sum(g.weight for g in v.groups if g.group in tie_groups) > 0.5 for v in me.vertices])
    strip = kdtree.KDTree(int(on_tie.sum()))
    for k, i in enumerate(np.where(on_tie)[0]):
        strip.insert(co[i], k)
    strip.balance()

    shirt = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)    # unfolded shirt faces under the tie
    beside = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # shirt faces beside the tie
    other = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)    # every other face
    front = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)    # faces of the front of the chest
    foreign = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)  # faces off the front of the chest
    folded = []                             # folded faces under the tie: (polygon, uv in texels)
    for poly in me.polygons:
        vs = list(poly.vertices)
        p = co[vs]
        t = np.array([uv[l].uv[:] for l in poly.loop_indices]) * size - 0.5
        body = not on_tie[vs].any()
        chest = (body and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y) and np.all((p[:, 2] > BOTTOM) & (p[:, 2] < TOP)))
        under = chest and np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < BOX_X) and strip.find(p.mean(axis=0))[2] < MARGIN
        on_front = chest and np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < CHEST_X)
        if np.ptp(t, axis=0).max() < 0.5:
            x, y = (min(max(int(round(c)), 0), n - 1) for c, n in zip(t.mean(axis=0), (w, h)))
            if under:
                folded.append((poly, t))
            else:
                other[y, x] = True
            (front if on_front else foreign)[y, x] = True
            continue
        for k in range(1, len(vs) - 1):
            cover = coverage(t[[0, k, k + 1]], w, h)
            if cover is None:
                continue
            (shirt if under else other)[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
            (front if on_front else foreign)[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
            if body and np.all((np.abs(p[:, 0]) > SIDE[0]) & (np.abs(p[:, 0]) < SIDE[1])) and chest \
                    and np.all((p[:, 2] > SIDE[2]) & (p[:, 2] < SIDE[3])):
                beside[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]

    # The shirt beside the tie: its black, normal, roughness and metal.
    dark = beside & ~shirt & (base.max(axis=-1) < 0.15)
    look = {k: np.median(px[k][dark], axis=0) for k in px}

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, repaints the textures packed in a Publisher .blend).

Paints the shirt under the tie plain black. When the tie was cut loose (build_rig.py, split_tie) the shirt under it
kept a tie-shaped patch: its faces were folded onto one texel of the chest, slightly grey, warm and with a tilted
normal, so it shows as a grey imprint of the tie whenever the tie swings away. This tool

- paints a square of texels around that texel with the black, the normal and the roughness of the shirt beside the
  tie (medians), as far as every texel in the square belongs to dark shirt faces only;
- paints the grey texels of the unfolded shirt faces under the tie black, never a texel that any other face (the tie
  strip, the knot, the collar, the skin, the jacket) uses, nor a coloured one (the gold of the knot).

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/plain_shirt.py -- <file.blend> [--write] [report.txt]

Without --write it only measures. The report gives the shirt texels before and after.
"""
import sys
from collections import Counter

import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import kdtree

# The chest under the tie, in Blender metres (he faces -Y). Above TOP the knot and the collar begin.
BOX_X, BOX_Y, BOTTOM, TOP = 0.16, -0.12, 1.30, 2.12
# A shirt face is under the tie if its centre lies this close (m) to a vert of the tie strip.
MARGIN = 0.04
# The shirt beside the tie that gives the black: |x| from, |x| to, z from, z to.
SIDE = (0.16, 0.26, 1.55, 2.00)
# The front of the chest between the lapels: texels of faces beyond it are never painted.
CHEST_X = 0.40
# A texel is off the black if a channel differs by more than this; grey if its channels differ by less than GREY.
PLAIN, GREY = 0.012, 0.05
# Half size (texels) of the square painted around the folded texel, at most: mip levels see this far.
SPOT = 8


def images(me):
    """The four textures of the material by their input on the shader."""
    found = {}
    for node in me.materials[0].node_tree.nodes:
        if node.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED":
            for name, socket in (("base", "Base Color"), ("rough", "Roughness"), ("metal", "Metallic")):
                link = node.inputs[socket].links
                if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                    found[name] = link[0].from_node.image
        if node.type == "NORMAL_MAP":
            link = node.inputs["Color"].links
            if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                found["normal"] = link[0].from_node.image
    if set(found) != {"base", "rough", "metal", "normal"}:
        raise RuntimeError("textures found: %s" % sorted(found))
    return found


def coverage(t, w, h):
    """Texels whose centre lies in a UV triangle given in texel units, plus a half-texel rim."""
    x0, y0 = np.floor(t.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
    x1, y1 = np.ceil(t.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
    d = (t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (t[0, 1] - t[2, 1])
    if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0 or abs(d) < 1e-9:
        return None
    xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
    b0 = ((t[1, 1] - t[2, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[2, 0] - t[1, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    b1 = ((t[2, 1] - t[0, 1]) * (xs - t[2, 0]) + (t[0, 0] - t[2, 0]) * (ys - t[2, 1])) / d
    tol = min(0.5, 1.0 / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
    return slice(y0, y1 + 1), slice(x0, x1 + 1), (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (1 - b0 - b1 >= -tol)


def stats(rgb, mask, black):
    part = rgb[mask]
    off = np.abs(part - black).max(axis=-1)
    return "%d texels, mean %s, brightest %.3f, off the black by > %.3f: %d" % (
        len(part), np.round(part.mean(axis=0), 4).tolist(), part.max(), PLAIN, int((off > PLAIN).sum()))


def main():
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
    path, write = args[0], "--write" in args
    report = next((a for a in args[1:] if a != "--write"), None)
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    me = mesh.data
    maps = images(me)
    w, h = maps["base"].size
    px = {k: np.array(im.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4) for k, im in maps.items()}
    size = np.array((w, h))
    co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
    uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
    tie_groups = {g.index for g in mesh.vertex_groups if g.name.startswith("tie_")}
    on_tie = np.array([sum(g.weight for g in v.groups if g.group in tie_groups) > 0.5 for v in me.vertices])
    strip = kdtree.KDTree(int(on_tie.sum()))
    for k, i in enumerate(np.where(on_tie)[0]):
        strip.insert(co[i], k)
    strip.balance()
    base = px["base"][..., :3]

    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    shirt = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # unfolded shirt faces under the tie
    beside = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)  # shirt faces beside the tie
    other = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)   # every other face
    foreign = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)  # faces off the front of the chest
    spots = Counter()
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        p = co[list(lt.vertices)]
        t = np.array([uv[l].uv[:] for l in lt.loops]) * size - 0.5
        body = not on_tie[list(lt.vertices)].any()
        under = (body and np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < BOX_X) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                 and np.all((p[:, 2] > BOTTOM) & (p[:, 2] < TOP)) and strip.find(p.mean(axis=0))[2] < MARGIN)
        front = (body and np.all(np.abs(p[:, 0]) < CHEST_X) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                 and np.all((p[:, 2] > BOTTOM) & (p[:, 2] < TOP)))
        cover = coverage(t, w, h)
        if cover is None or np.ptp(t, axis=0).max() < 0.5:
            x, y = (min(max(int(round(c)), 0), n - 1) for c, n in zip(t.mean(axis=0), (w, h)))
            if under:
                spots[(y, x)] += 1
            else:
                other[y, x] = True
                foreign[y, x] |= not front
            continue
        (shirt if under else other)[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
        if not front:
            foreign[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]
        side = (body and np.all((np.abs(p[:, 0]) > SIDE[0]) & (np.abs(p[:, 0]) < SIDE[1])) and np.all(p[:, 1] < BOX_Y)
                and np.all((p[:, 2] > SIDE[2]) & (p[:, 2] < SIDE[3])))
        if side:
            beside[cover[0], cover[1]] |= cover[2]

    # The shirt beside the tie: its black, normal and roughness.
    dark = beside & ~shirt & (base.max(axis=-1) < 0.15)
    look = {k: np.median(px[k][..., :3][dark], axis=0) for k in ("base", "normal", "rough", "metal")}
    black = look["base"]
    lines = ["%s" % path, "shirt beside the tie, %d texels (spread %.4f): %s" % (
        dark.sum(), base[dark].std(axis=0).max(),
        ", ".join("%s %s" % (k, np.round(v, 3).tolist()) for k, v in look.items()))]

    # The texels the folded faces under the tie point at; a gold one belongs to the knot and stays.
    paint = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    for (y, x), n in spots.most_common():
        c = base[y, x]
        if c.max() - c.min() > GREY:
            lines.append("folded spot (%d, %d), %d faces: coloured %s, left alone" % (x, y, n, np.round(c, 3).tolist()))
            continue
        # The square grows while every texel in it is dark and used by faces of the front of the chest only, or by
        # none: no tie, no knot, no collar, no skin, no jacket.
        r = 0
        while r < SPOT:
            q = (slice(max(y - r - 1, 0), y + r + 2), slice(max(x - r - 1, 0), x + r + 2))
            used = other[q] | shirt[q]
            if (used & (base[q].max(axis=-1) > 0.15)).any() or foreign[q].any():
                break
            r += 1
        paint[max(y - r, 0):y + r + 1, max(x - r, 0):x + r + 1] = True
        lines.append("folded spot (%d, %d), %d faces: base %s normal %s rough %.3f, square of %d texels" % (
            x, y, n, np.round(c, 3).tolist(), np.round(px["normal"][y, x, :3], 3).tolist(), px["rough"][y, x, 0],
            (2 * r + 1) ** 2))
    grey = shirt & ~other & (base.max(axis=-1) - base.min(axis=-1) < GREY) & (base.max(axis=-1) < 0.5)
    paint_grey = grey & (np.abs(base - black).max(axis=-1) > PLAIN)
    lines.append("unfolded shirt under the tie: %d texels (%d shared with other faces), %d grey off the black" % (
        (shirt & ~other).sum(), (shirt & other).sum(), paint_grey.sum()))
    every = paint | paint_grey
    lines.append("before: " + stats(base, every, black))
    if write:
        base[every] = black
        px["normal"][..., :3][paint] = look["normal"]
        px["rough"][..., :3][paint] = look["rough"]
        for k, im in maps.items():
            im.pixels.foreach_set(px[k].ravel())
            im.update()
            im.pack()
        lines.append("after:  " + stats(base, every, black))
        bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()
        lines.append("saved")
    print("\n".join("[shirt] " + l for l in lines))
    if report:
        with open(report, "w") as out:
            out.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# KIND: offline tool. Rebuilds the Publisher rig and its clips from the Meshy files, then reports the skin tears of
# one pose.
#   bash Tools/Art/publisher_rig/rebuild.sh <work_dir> [clip=Idle] [frame=1]
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)"
BLENDER="${BLENDER:-/f/Program Files/Blender Foundation/Blender 5.2/blender.exe}"
OUT="$1"; CLIP="${2:-Idle}"; FRAME="${3:-1}"
FIXED="$ROOT/Art/Models/boss_fixed"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
"$BLENDER" -b --factory-startup --python "$HERE/build_rig.py" > "$OUT/build.log" 2>&1
"$BLENDER" -b --factory-startup --python "$HERE/rework_clips.py" -- "$FIXED/publisher_rig.blend" "$FIXED/publisher_clips.blend" "$FIXED/clips.json" "$OUT/rework.txt" > "$OUT/rework.log" 2>&1
"$BLENDER" -b --factory-startup --python "$HERE/find_tears.py" -- "$FIXED/publisher_clips.blend" "$OUT/tears.txt" "$CLIP" "$FRAME" > "$OUT/tears.log" 2>&1
grep "\[build\]" "$OUT/build.log" || true
head -12 "$OUT/tears.txt"

Done and committed on main as `f3a5269`. The main session's uncommitted Source changes were left out. The DEVLOG line asks the main session to reimport the Publisher with `import_models.py` (`JAM_IMPORT_ONLY=Publisher`) before its next package.

- **The cause wasn't the paint itself.** The shirt faces under the tie were all pointed at a single "plain black" pixel of the texture. That pixel sits on a black strip 2–3 pixels wide between cream jacket pixels. When the texture is shown smaller, at a distance, it blends with the jacket, so the area under the tie came out grey (0.57 when averaged over 16×16 pixels).
- **What I did instead of repainting:** painting couldn't fix it without changing the jacket. So I pointed those 1011 shirt-face corners at the middle of a 51×51 pixel patch of plain shirt black, and painted the 13 grey shirt pixels under the tie black. Measured on the shirt under the tie: 0.059 before, 0.043 after at every size, the same as the shirt beside the tie. The close-up render with the tie hidden shows no grey tie shape any more.
- **Nothing else changed.** I compared against the previously committed `.blend`: same mesh, normal, roughness and metallic maps unchanged, base colour changed only in those 13 pixels. The tie, gold knot, collar border and skin are untouched.
- **Export:** re-exported the same way as before and read back, failed: 0. The new `SK_Publisher.fbx` uses the new spot (1011 corners). The fix lives in `Tools/Art/publisher_rig/plain_shirt.py`, and `rebuild.sh` now runs it. I didn't check anything in Unreal and didn't open the editor.
- **Leftover:** the black collar around the neck still uses that same black strip pixel, so it may also turn grey at a distance. I left it alone because you said the collar border must not change.

Next step: the main session reimports the Publisher. If the collar also looks grey after that, I can move it to the plain black patch the same way.

entries.name: mcp__hyper3d__rodin_create_uploads
entries.description: Create one-hour presigned PUT URLs for one batch of files of the same kind. kind defaults to image: 1-5 images (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, TIFF, AVIF or HEIC), at most 25 MiB each, for rodin_generate.reference_upload_ids or rodin_generate_agentic.reference_upload_ids. kind=model: one mesh (GLB, OBJ, STL, FBX or USD), at most 128 MiB, for rodin_generate_rigging.model_upload_id. kind=animation: 1-10 FBX files, at most 25 MiB each, for rodin_generate_rigging.animation_upload_ids; each FBX must contain exactly one animation clip (Take). PUT exactly size_bytes bytes with the returned headers before passing an ID to generation. The format is detected from the uploaded bytes. An uploaded ID can be reused by later generations until it expires, so do not upload the same file twice. If you cannot complete the HTTP PUT uploads, explain the limitation to the user in their language and suggest continuing at https://hyper3d.ai. In ChatGPT Chat mode, also suggest trying Work mode.

kind.description: Kind of every file in the batch. Defaults to image.

filename.description: Filename without a directory path. OBJ, STL and USDZ meshes need their extension.

size_bytes.description: Exact file size in bytes, within the limit of its kind.

files.description: One batch of the selected kind: 1-5 images, 1 model or 1-10 animations.

entries.name: mcp__hyper3d__rodin_generate
entries.description: Use this tool for text-only generation or image-based subjects whose defining geometry is not well suited to procedural n-gons modeling, such as detailed sculpted characters, garments, or realistic car bodies. Prefer rodin_generate_agentic for subjects with clear geometric construction, even when the image shows a single, clear object. For multi-view collages or design concept sheets, first crop the relevant views locally into separate reference images with one clear subject per image, or use rodin_generate_agentic directly; image layout alone does not determine the best tool. Start a Rodin Gen-2.5 generation from a non-empty prompt, one or more reference images, or both. At least one of prompt or reference_upload_ids is required. texture_delight defaults to false; setting it to true is recommended when reference images contain highly reflective surfaces. This consumes credits. The response includes display_url; present that URL only after the generation completes. If this call times out, do not retry it automatically; ask the user to check Hyper3D Mine.

prompt.description: A non-empty text description. Required when reference_upload_ids is omitted.

reference_upload_ids.description: One to five uploaded reference image IDs. Required when prompt is omitted.

texture_delight.description: Enable texture de-lighting. Defaults to false; recommended when reference images contain highly reflective surfaces.

quality_override.description: Target polygon count. Raw accepts 500 to 1,000,000; Quad accepts 1,000 to 50,000.

entries.name: mcp__hyper3d__rodin_get_result
entries.description: Return a permanent Hyper3D result page plus temporary signed URLs for permitted Rodin output files. When presenting a link to the user, always use display_url and never expose files[].url. Only use files[].url to download a file when the user explicitly asks.

entries.name: mcp__hyper3d__rodin_get_status
entries.description: Read the state of a generation. When no job records remain, downloadable model files indicate completed; otherwise the state is unknown. stage contains a user-facing name plus a 1-based current position and stable total; current is 0 before the first stage starts.

entries.name: mcp__hyper3d__rodin_list_uploads
entries.description: List files the user saved in their Hyper3D library, newest first. Pass returned upload_id values instead of uploading the same files again: kind=animation to rodin_generate_rigging.animation_upload_ids, kind=model to rodin_generate_rigging.model_upload_id, kind=image to reference_upload_ids. Reads the library only and does not consume credits.

tag.description: Only files carrying this exact tag.

entries.name: mcp__hyper3d__rodin_wait
entries.description: Wait up to 45 seconds for a terminal state; unknown also ends the wait. A timeout returns the latest state and does not mean generation failed. Progress is reported as stage name/current/total, not a percentage.
